history.summary: Goa's oldest surviving temple and its only intact Kadamba-Yadava structure, built of black basalt carried from the Deccan plateau. Its remote clearing deep in the Bhagwan Mahaveer Wildlife Sanctuary saved it from destruction during Muslim and Portuguese rule; it is an ASI-protected Monument of National Importance and an active worship site. Legend attributes it to a Kadamba queen, Kamladevi (unverified). Features: east-facing garbhagriha, basalt-pillared Nandi mandapa with a headless Nandi, bas-reliefs of Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma with consorts, and the Kadamba elephant-trampling-horse emblem on a pillar base. name: Tambdi Surla Mahadev Temple
town_description: Tambdi Surla is a small forest village in Sanguem taluka, South Goa, on the edge of the Bhagwan Mahaveer Wildlife Sanctuary and Mollem National Park near the Karnataka border; its name comes from the area's red (tambdi) soil.

travel.airport: Goa International Airport (Dabolim), about 65 km / ~2 hours by road
travel.road: Via Molem/Dharbandora off the Anmod Ghat road, or 22 km south of Valpoi; forest road through the sanctuary

visitor_information.best_time: Monsoon and winter (June to February) for the forest setting; October to March generally
visitor_information.opening_hours: 08:30-17:30 per Tripadvisor listing (one source cites 07:30-17:30) — verify locally
